Definition: from G4716; to impale on the cross; figuratively, to extinguish (subdue) passion or selfishness:--crucify.
BiblicalUsage: To crucify is the act that stands at the centre of the faith. The chief priests cry, Crucify him, crucify him; Peter tells the house of Israel that God hath made that same Jesus, whom ye have crucified, both Lord and Christ; they that are Christ's have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts; and Paul glories in the cross, by whom the world is crucified unto me, and I unto the world.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the cross is both what was done to Christ and what He does to me: He was crucified, and by His cross my flesh is crucified too. I hold that the world crucified to me is the freedom Paul boasts in.
